governance.gasoline_exclusion_evidence: No gasoline record appears in this file. The Isuzu gasoline line for the period (NPR / NPR-HD with the GM Vortec 6000 6.0L V8 and later the GM L8T 6.6L V8) was identified in the same sources and deliberately left out; see docs/hermes/ISUZU_US_DIESEL_CLOSURE_2000_2026.md.

evidence_status_meanings.VERIFIED: An Isuzu Commercial Truck of America source published in or for that model year names the model and its diesel engine.
evidence_status_meanings.PARTIAL: Isuzu evidence names the model for the model year but leaves at least one required field (engine code, displacement or configuration) unproven for that exact year.
evidence_status_meanings.UNRESOLVED: No Isuzu source retrieved in this closure covers that model year.
evidence_status_meanings.CONFLICTING: Two sources disagree; both are recorded and the disagreement is listed in conflicts.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The Isuzu NPR Diesel specification page captured 2000-10-18 publishes NPR DIESEL at 12,000 lbs GVWR and NPR HD DIESEL at 14,500 lbs GVWR, both with Engine -Type 'Turbo/Intercooled Diesel/4HE1-TC' and -Displacement '4.75 L (290 CID)'. NHTSA vPIC lists NPR/NPR-HD for both model years.
year_blocks.status_note: MY2001 rests on the October 2000 page plus the NHTSA MY2001 listing; the 2001 capture of nprdspecs.htm could not be retrieved, so no Isuzu document published inside calendar 2001 was read.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: NHTSA vPIC lists NQR for model years 2000 and 2001, but no Isuzu Commercial Truck of America document covering NQR in those years was retrieved. The earliest Isuzu NQR evidence in this closure is the 2002-06-04 capture.
year_blocks.status_note: Deliberately left UNRESOLVED rather than back-filled from the 2002 NQR page, which would be an unproven continuity assumption.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The NPR and NQR diesel specification pages captured in April 2002, February 2003 and February 2004 all publish 4HE1-TC. The Crew Cab specification page captured 2002-04-09 publishes Crew Cab for NPR, NPR HD and NQR with the same engine. NHTSA vPIC lists NPR/NPR-HD and NQR for all three model years.
year_blocks.status_note: Crew Cab is evidenced for 2002 directly; for 2003 and 2004 the crewcabspecs captures of 2003-02-06 and 2004-02-18 carry the same content.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: Isuzu published an NRR Diesel specification page at 19,500 lbs GVWR with 4HK1-TC 5.2L on 2004-03-22, one month after its NPR and NQR pages still published 4HE1-TC. NHTSA vPIC does not list NRR before model year 2005.

year_blocks.engine_description: Inline 4 cylinder, direct injection, turbocharged and intercooled
year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: From the January 2005 capture onward every Isuzu N-Series diesel specification page publishes 4HK1-TC in place of 4HE1-TC, and NRR joins NPR, NPR HD and NQR in the N-Series navigation. The 4H engine page captured 2006-08-24 gives bore x stroke 115 x 125 mm, 5193 cc (317 cu.in). The 2006 and 2007 NPR owner's manuals cover the same vehicles.
year_blocks.configuration_note: From model year 2007 these vehicles carry a Diesel Particulate Filter; see the 2007 emissions cut in the generations file.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The N-Series diesel specification pages captured through 2011, 2012, 2013 and the 2014-03-25 index publish NPR-HD, NQR and NRR with 4HK1-TC.
year_blocks.status_note: MY2014 rests on the 2014-03-25 index listing the models; the model-year 2014 engine statement was read from the 2013 and 2015 specification pages rather than a 2014-dated engine page.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The Isuzu press release of 2010-03-09 states that the 12,000-lbs GVWR NPR ECO-MAX is a 2011 model year truck powered by the 4JJ1-TC, 150 hp, 282 lb-ft, and that this is the first use of the 4J family in the U.S. market. The N-Series diesel specification pages captured from 2013 to 2018-02-16 continue to publish 4JJ1-TC alongside 4HK1-TC. The 2019-04-21 capture lists the 4HK1-TC as the only diesel engine, which ends the block.
year_blocks.status_note: This is a separate diesel powertrain from the 4HK1-TC and must never inherit 4HK1-TC filters. It is the only 3.0L diesel in the USA N-Series line.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: NPR-XD appears for the first time in the Isuzu specification index captured 2015-04-04 and in its own specification sheet captured 2015-03-14; the equivalent 2014-03-25 index lists only NPR, NPR-HD, NQR and NRR. From 2015 to 2018 the N-Series diesel pages publish NPR-HD, NPR-XD, NQR and NRR with 4HK1-TC.

The N-Series diesel page captured 2019-04-21 publishes 'Isuzu 4HK1-TC 5.2 liter diesel engine' as the only diesel engine and lists NPR-HD 14,500/20,500, NPR-XD 16,000/22,000, NQR 17,950/23,950 and NRR 19,500/25,500. The full-line brochure with Copyright 2019 carries a '2020 ISUZU N-SERIES DIESEL: NPR-HD / NPR-XD / NQR / NRR' section.
year_blocks.status_note: MY2021 is carried by the 2021 captures of the individual npr-hd, npr-xd, nqr and nrr specification sheets, which publish the same four models and the same engine but print no model year.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: Carried forward unchanged from the existing repository matrix config/isuzu-n-series-us-oem-matrix.json, whose MY2022-MY2024 rows were already closed as OEM_VERIFIED against the 2022, 2023 and 2024 Isuzu brochures.

The 2026 pocket guide and the current N-Series diesel specification page publish NPR-HD 14,500, NPR-XD 16,000, NRR Derate 17,950 and NRR 19,500 lbs GVWR, all with Isuzu 4HK1-TC 5.2L (317 cu. in.), 215 hp @ 2,500 rpm, 452 lb-ft @ 1,850 rpm, in Standard Cab and Crew Cab. NRR Derate is a PIO option, not a separate chassis.

model_retirement.NQR: Not published in the MY2025 or MY2026 diesel line-up; NRR Derate at 17,950 lbs GVWR occupies the former NQR rating.

year_blocks.configuration_note: NRR DERATE is a production-installed-option derate of the NRR to 17,950 lbs GVWR. It shares the NRR chassis and powertrain and is recorded as a configuration-level identity, not a new engine.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The individual FRR, FSR, FTR and FVR specification pages captured in 2000 and 2001, the F-Series index captured 2002-03-23 and the F-Series specification PDF captured 2003-12-10 all publish the same four models with 6HK1-TC 7.8L (475 CID), 200 HP @ 2400 rpm (FVR 230 HP). The 1998 capture of the same FRR page still published 6HE1-TC and the 1999 capture already published 6HK1-TC, which dates the engine change to before this scope opens.
year_blocks.gvwr_note: FRR is published at both 18,000 and 19,500 lbs and FTR at both 25,950 and 30,000 lbs; the table above records the higher published rating for each.
year_blocks.configuration_note: F-Series in this period is an air-braked chassis; the FTR page publishes air brakes.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The FXR specification page captured 2004-04-05 publishes FXR at 33,001 lbs GVWR with 6HK1-TC and shows FRR, FSR, FTR, FVR and FXR together in the F-Series navigation. The 2005 capture of the F-Series index publishes the same five models.
year_blocks.discovery_note: FXR is not in the manifest's candidate_model_names list. It was found in Isuzu's own published F-Series line and is recorded here because the candidate list is a search aid, not a scope boundary.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: From the 2006 capture onward the Isuzu F-Series pages publish only FTR, FVR and FXR; FRR and FSR are gone. The 6H engine page captured 2006-09-03 gives 6HK1-TC 7.8L. The FTR, FVR and FXR pages captured through 2010 continue to publish the same three models and engine.
year_blocks.configuration_note: From model year 2007 these vehicles carry a Diesel Particulate Filter, per the Isuzu 2007 emissions brochure covering both the 4H and the 6H engines.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: Every /fseries/ specification page captured in 2011 and 2012 returns the Isuzu error page, and the site navigation of those captures lists N-SERIES and REACH VAN with no F-SERIES entry. The 2014 and 2015 captures of the same URL serve N-Series content. NHTSA vPIC lists no F-Series designation for Isuzu between model years 2011 and 2016.
year_blocks.status_note: VERIFIED_ABSENT records a model year in which Isuzu USA published no F-Series diesel truck. It is a closed answer, not a gap.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The F-Series brochure captured 2016-03-31 with Copyright 2016 announces 'Isuzu's Newest Family Member - the Isuzu FTR', a Class 6 LCF truck with a 5.2L diesel engine, rear air brake and Allison 2000 Series. NHTSA vPIC first lists FTR for model year 2017. The MY2021 FTR brochure publishes 25,950 lbs GVWR, 30,000 lbs GCWR, DIESEL 5.2 L, 215 HP @ 2,500 RPM, 520 lb-ft @ 1,600 RPM.
year_blocks.status_note: MY2018 is PARTIAL because no brochure or specification sheet dated to model year 2018 was retrieved; the model and engine for 2018 rest on the surrounding 2017 and 2019 Isuzu documents.
year_blocks.engine_note: This FTR is a 5.2L four-cylinder, not the 7.8L six of the 2000-2010 F-Series. A 2000-2010 FTR filter set must never be applied to a 2017-2021 FTR.

year_blocks.exact_evidence_summary: The 2022 F-Series specification brochure publishes FTR at 25,950 lbs GVWR, FVR at 25,950 lbs GVWR and FVR at 33,000 lbs GVWR, all with the B6.7L diesel engine. The 2025 brochure names the three models as Class 6 FTR (25,950 lbs. GVWR), Class 6 FVR Derate (25,950 lbs. GVWR) and Class 7 FVR (33,000 lbs. GVWR) and states that every Isuzu F-Series truck has a Cummins B6.7 diesel engine, 260 horsepower and 660 lb-ft through an Allison 2000-series RDS automatic, with eight wheelbases from 152 to 248 inches and a 50- or 100-gallon fuel tank.
year_blocks.engine_note: This is the only non-Isuzu diesel engine in the closure. Its filtration is a Cummins engine platform and must be resolved on Cummins/Isuzu evidence, never inherited from the 6HK1-TC or 4HK1-TC F-Series.

conflicts.subject: First model year of the N-Series NRR in the USA

position_a.weight: Isuzu primary, but the page prints no model year

position_b.weight: manufacturer-submitted federal record, corroboration tier only

conflicts.assessment: The NRR page was published 2004-03-22, while the NPR page of 2004-02-07 and the NQR page of 2004-02-18 still published 4HE1-TC. A spring publication of the first 4HK1-TC model is equally consistent with an early MY2005 launch. Not resolved on the evidence retrieved.
conflicts.resolution: UNRESOLVED. MY2004 NRR is recorded as CONFLICTING. MY2005 onward is VERIFIED. No filter set is attached to a MY2004 NRR.

conflicts.subject: First model year of the current F-Series FVR in the USA

position_a.claim: FVR listed for model years 2020 and 2021

position_b.claim: FVR is introduced with the 2022 F-Series
position_b.weight: Isuzu primary, explicitly dated to model year 2022

conflicts.assessment: No Isuzu document retrieved publishes an FVR for model year 2020 or 2021; the MY2021 F-Series brochure publishes FTR alone. Isuzu's own dated evidence is preferred over the vPIC listing.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED in favour of Isuzu. FVR and FVR Derate start at MY2022. The vPIC MY2020/2021 FVR rows are recorded here and not acted on.

excluded_from_scope.subject: Isuzu NRR EV
excluded_from_scope.reason: Battery-electric, not diesel. Published by Isuzu for MY2025 and MY2026 and out of this fuel scope.

excluded_from_scope.subject: Isuzu REACH van
excluded_from_scope.reason: Walk-in van body on the N-Series chassis; not resolved in this closure and not one of the manifest's candidate families.

excluded_from_scope.subject: Isuzu H-Series
excluded_from_scope.reason: Appears in the isuzucv.com navigation between the 2006 and 2009 captures and in NHTSA vPIC for MY2005-2008. No Isuzu specification page for it was retrieved, so it is neither included nor denied. Recorded as an open discovery item.

excluded_from_scope.subject: Isuzu i-280, i-290, i-350, i-370, Ascender, Rodeo, Trooper, Axiom, VehiCross, Hombre
excluded_from_scope.reason: Light-duty passenger and pickup models in the vPIC listing, not commercial trucks.

open_discovery_items.question: Did Isuzu Commercial Truck of America sell a diesel H-Series commercial truck in the USA between MY2005 and MY2008, and with which engine?
The manifest lists FBR as a candidate. No Isuzu USA source retrieved in this closure publishes an FBR.
Isuzu evidence for the NQR diesel in MY2000 and MY2001.
